lessonRef.subject: ready-for-life
lessonRef.unitTitle: Time, Belongings, and Asking for Help
lessonRef.title: Mastery check: asking for help clearly

standardsRefs: Manuel Academy Ready for Life elementary sequence — Grade 3
Ready for Life v1 safety, supervision, and no-shame policy reference
Manuel Academy RFL G3 Unit 5 — time, belongings, and help-seeking
objective: Learners ask a trusted adult for help with one real, current question or problem using a three-part structure: naming the specific problem, saying what they already tried, and stating exactly what kind of help they need, so the adult can respond without having to guess.
scenario: When a genuine question or stuck point comes up today, such as an instruction the learner does not understand or a job they cannot finish alone, the learner finds a trusted adult, uses the three-part structure out loud, and the adult confirms afterward whether the request was clear enough to act on right away.
safetyNotes: A trusted adult confirms that the help-asking moment actually happened as described, not only that the learner reports it happened.

simulationAlternative.description: If no real question or stuck point comes up today, the learner instead role-plays the three-part ask-for-help structure with a trusted adult, using a real, specific situation recalled from earlier in the week instead of a live one.

materials: a real, current question or stuck point

tasks.directions: Before asking anyone, think through the three parts of the structure on your own.

prompts.text: Write the specific problem you have right now, in one sentence.

tasks.directions: Approach a trusted adult and use all three parts of the structure out loud, in order, before pausing for their response.

prompts.text: I named the specific problem, not just a general 'I'm stuck.'
I said what I already tried before asking for help.
I stated exactly what kind of help I needed, such as an explanation, a demonstration, or a decision.
I asked a trusted adult directly, out loud, instead of waiting to be noticed.

tasks.directions: Later today or tomorrow, use the same three-part structure again with a second, different question, to check whether the structure holds up more than once.

prompts.text: Describe the second question you asked and name which of the three parts you remembered on your own, without checking a written reminder.

tasks.directions: Think about the help you actually received compared to the help you asked for.

prompts.text: Describe the specific kind of help your adult gave you, such as an explanation, a demonstration, or a decision, and whether it matched what you asked for.

remediation: If a learner states the problem vaguely, such as 'I don't get it,' without saying what was already tried or what help is needed, causing the adult to have to ask follow-up questions, reteach with a fill-in-the-blank sentence frame practiced once on a low-stakes made-up question before using it on a real one.
extension: Have the learner use the same three-part structure to ask a co-op teacher or another trusted adult outside the household for help with a different kind of question, showing the structure transfers beyond the household.
